overall_assessment: Anonymization works well for NIH: none of the 21 packet courses (all random controls; the pre-pass flagged nothing) contains staff names, e-mails, phone numbers or administrative dates, and no course content was removed (unyeared 'vårsemesteret', '80 %', '6000-8000 ord', 'APA-manual (7. utg.)' all kept). The only removals are the '(Høst 2025)' title stamp and the semester-year on the reading-list link line, which leaves a cosmetic dangling 'Pensumlista for.' in most plans.

findings.description: The reading-list link text 'Pensumlista for høsten 2025.' / 'Pensumliste for høsten 2025 og våren 2026.' correctly loses its semester-year, but the preposition stays, so the line reads 'Pensumlista for.' — a half-removed phrase. Cosmetic: no personal data and no plan content involved (the actual reading list is not in the extracted text at all).
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The generic season+year rule in .anon_generic() (R/anonymize.R, the 'høsten 2025' / 'våren2026' inflected-season pattern) removes the season-year and any 'og <season> <year>' list but not the preceding 'for'.
findings.suggested_fix: In .anon_generic(), before the generic season-year removal, drop a leading 'for ' when the season-year ends the sentence: str_remove_all("(?i)\\s+for\\s+(?:høsten|våren|haust(?:en)?)\\s*\\d{4}(?:\\s+og\\s+(?:høsten|våren|haust(?:en)?)\\s*\\d{4})?(?=\\.)") so the line becomes 'Pensumlista.'; add a test in tests/testthat/test-anonymize.R with 'Pensumlista for høsten 2025.' and 'Pensumliste for høsten 2025 og våren 2026.'.
